fields.meta_title: Personal Training Intake Form Builder | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a personal training intake form with goals, training history, available days, and a PAR-Q+ step, sent to the right trainer. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Personal Training Intake Form for the First Session
fields.hero_description: Build a personal training intake form that collects goals, available days, and PAR-Q+ answers before the first session.
fields.features_heading: What the Trainer Knows Before the First Rep
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds the intake around the client's goal and schedule, and the screening answers stay inside the app.
fields.feature_1:
Questions that follow the goal

A client who picks strength is asked which lifts they do now and how many days they train. Pick a race instead, and the form asks for the race date and weekly mileage.
fields.feature_2:
The PAR-Q+ as its own step

The first page of the official PAR-Q+ holds seven general health questions. A Yes to any of them opens the follow-up pages, and the client signs the declaration on screen.
fields.feature_3:
Available days, picked as checkboxes

Clients tick the mornings and evenings they can train, then request up to three time slots for session one. The trainer sees every request on one screen, by start date.
fields.feature_4:
Alerts that say an intake is ready

The trainer gets an email or a Slack message with the client's name and a note that the intake is ready. Screening answers stay out of the message and wait in the app.
fields.feature_5:
Client records in a database you own

Every intake is saved as a row in a database you own, searchable by client and by trainer. With no response caps, a month of heavy sign-ups runs through the same intake form.
fields.feature_6:
Code you can take elsewhere

On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository when the intake has to sit inside a member app you already run. Host it where you like and keep building.
fields.why_title: Why Build Your Training Intake With Emergent?
fields.why_description: A paper intake gets read in the lobby before the warm-up. One filled out at home reaches the trainer the day before.

fields.tab_content_1:
Seven No answers, and session one is requested

Corwin Kerrane signs up at Ironwhistle Strength. He picks strength as his goal, notes 2 years of lifting at a home gym, and answers No to all seven PAR-Q+ questions. He signs the declaration and requests Tuesday, Thursday, and Saturday at 6 AM. Trainer Liesel Lartey gets an email that his intake is ready.
fields.tab_content_2:
Session one waits while a trainer reads one Yes

Gannet Fitness screens every new member with the PAR-Q+. Philippa Dulac answers Yes to one question on the first page, and the form opens the follow-up pages. Her intake reads Needs review, and her first session stays unbooked. Trainer Oskar Ferrante gets a Slack message that a new intake needs his review, with no answers in it.
fields.tab_content_3:
Two dumbbells, one pull-up bar, no bench, all on file

Marisela Quill coaches every client by video, and her intake asks what equipment each one has at home. Bastian Greaves lists two adjustable dumbbells up to 50 lb and one pull-up bar, with No bench checked. He picks Monday and Wednesday at 7 PM for calls. Marisela reads the list the day before and plans a program with no bench work.
fields.tab_content_4:
One of four trainers fits fat loss after 6 PM

Wyncote Athletic Club has four trainers, and its intake asks every new member for a goal and a time slot. Henrietta Sowande picks fat loss and evenings after 6 PM. Dashiell Okoye is the one of the four who coaches fat loss in that slot, and her intake goes to him. He gets an email that it is ready and calls her the next day.

plan.angle: Template sites for personal training intake form hand over a printable list of questions. This page shows a trainer the intake running in four real setups: a private studio where a client answers No to all seven PAR-Q+ questions and his first session request lands on the trainer's screen, a gym where one Yes opens the follow-up pages and holds the first session for a trainer's review, an online coach who gets a client's home equipment before the first video call, and a club where the goal and the time slot pick the trainer. Health answers stay in the app; alerts only say an intake is ready.
